## Summary
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noUselessQualifier`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-qualifier`](https://typescript-eslint.io/rules/no-unnecessary-qualifier)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noUselessQualifier": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow unnecessary namespace and enum qualifiers.

The members of a TypeScript namespace or enum are usually accessed through
the name of the namespace or enum, for example `Direction.Up`. The
`Direction.` part is called a qualifier.

Inside the namespace or enum itself, the members can be used by their name
alone, so the qualifier only repeats what is already known.

This rule doesn't report a qualifier when the member name alone would refer
to something else, for example because a local variable has the same name.

## Examples

### Invalid

```ts
enum Direction {
    Up,
    Down = Direction.Up + 1,
}
```

### Valid

```ts
enum Direction {
    Up,
    Down = Up + 1,
}

namespace Shapes {
    export type Point = { x: number; y: number };
    const origin: Point = { x: 0, y: 0 };
}

namespace Outer {
    export type Id = number;
    namespace Inner {
        type Id = string;
        // `Id` alone would refer to `Inner.Id`.
        const id: Outer.Id = 0;
    }
}
```
